findings.title: applyFilterExpression executes arbitrary user input via eval — no test covers any path
findings.why: The entire function is a single eval() call on a caller-controlled string. No test exercises it at all: not the happy path, not a benign expression, not a malicious payload. An attacker who can reach POST /notes/filter can execute arbitrary Python in the server process. The absence of tests also means no one has verified that 'simple predicates' actually work or fail gracefully.
findings.evidence:
def applyFilterExpression(notes, expression):
    return [n for n in notes if eval(expression)]
findings.fix:
test_applyFilterExpression_simple_predicate — call applyFilterExpression([(1,'a','b'),(2,'c','d')], 'n[0] == 1') and assert only the first tuple is returned.
test_applyFilterExpression_code_injection — pass expression='__import__("os").system("id")' and assert a ValueError/TypeError is raised (once the function is fixed to use a safe AST evaluator); until fixed, this test documents the live RCE path.
test_filter_notes_route_eval_rejected — POST /notes/filter with a system-call expression and assert the server returns 400, not 200 or 500.

findings.title: current_user_id never verifies the token signature — no test exists
findings.why: The function splits the token on '.' and returns int(parts[1]) without checking the SHA-1 prefix against any known secret. Any caller can forge a token of the form '<garbage>.<target_user_id>' and impersonate any user. The function was changed from the prior design (plain query-param) and is now the sole identity gate for /notes/search and /notes (POST), yet has zero test coverage.
findings.fix:
test_current_user_id_valid_token — call issue_token(42), pass the result to current_user_id, assert 42 is returned.
test_current_user_id_forged_token — pass 'deadbeef.99' (fabricated prefix, not produced by issue_token) and assert None is returned (documents that forged tokens must be rejected once the function is fixed).
test_current_user_id_missing_token — pass None and assert None.
test_current_user_id_malformed_token — pass 'notadottoken' and assert None.

findings.title: isAdmin uses a hardcoded plaintext bypass token — no test exists
findings.why: ADMIN_BYPASS_TOKEN is the literal string 'letmein-admin' committed in config.py. isAdmin() grants full admin rights to anyone who sends this header value. There is no test that (a) confirms a correct token grants access, (b) confirms any other value is denied, or (c) catches the trivially-guessable value at review time.
findings.fix:
test_isAdmin_correct_token — pass headers containing X-Admin-Token: letmein-admin and assert True.
test_isAdmin_wrong_token — pass X-Admin-Token: wrong and assert False.
test_isAdmin_missing_header — pass empty headers and assert False.
test_remove_note_route_forbidden — DELETE /notes/1 without the header, assert 403.
test_remove_note_route_admin_allowed — DELETE /notes/1 with the correct header, assert 204.

findings.title: issue_token has no tests — output format and round-trip correctness unverified
findings.why: issue_token() is the only token-minting function and is depended upon by current_user_id() for the expected token format. No test verifies the output structure (hex.user_id), that the user_id round-trips correctly, or that tokens for different users are distinct. If the format drifts, the already-broken signature check in current_user_id would silently fail.
findings.fix:
test_issue_token_format — call issue_token(7), assert the result matches r'^[0-9a-f]{40}\.7$'.
test_issue_token_different_users_differ — assert issue_token(1) != issue_token(2).
test_issue_token_round_trip — call issue_token(5), pass result to current_user_id, assert 5 is returned (will fail until TST-2 is fixed, making the gap visible).

findings.title: search_notes switched from parameterised query to f-string — SQL injection path is untested
findings.why: The previous implementation used '?' placeholders (parameterised). This PR replaces it with an f-string that interpolates user_id and query directly into the SQL string. Because current_user_id() returns int(parts[1]) from an unverified token, an attacker controls user_id. A crafted query value also injects into the LIKE clause. Neither injection vector has a test.
findings.evidence:
sql = f"SELECT id, title, body FROM notes WHERE user_id = {user_id} AND title LIKE '%{query}%'"
cur.execute(sql)
findings.fix:
test_search_notes_sql_injection_query — call search_notes("' OR '1'='1", 1) against a test DB and assert only the expected rows are returned, not all rows.
test_search_notes_sql_injection_user_id — call search_notes("", "1 OR 1=1") and assert a parameterisation error or empty result, not all rows.
test_search_notes_normal — insert a known row and assert search_notes('hello', user_id) returns it.

findings.title: delete_note is a new function with no tests — SQL injection and silent-failure paths uncovered
findings.why: delete_note() is entirely new and has no tests at all. It uses an f-string for the note_id in a DELETE statement, making it injectable. It also swallows all exceptions silently ('except: pass'), so callers (including the route) can never observe a failure. Neither the happy path (row deleted), the no-op path (non-existent id), nor the error path is exercised.
findings.fix:
test_delete_note_deletes_row — insert a note, call delete_note(note_id), query the DB directly, assert the row is gone.
test_delete_note_nonexistent_id — call delete_note(99999) against an empty DB, assert no exception is raised and no rows affected.
test_delete_note_sql_injection — call delete_note("1 OR 1=1") and assert a parameterisation error is raised (documents the injection; will pass once fixed to use parameterised queries).

findings.title: POST /notes/filter route has no tests — eval reachable over HTTP, error trace exposed
findings.why: The route is entirely new and untested. It chains two already-untested vulnerabilities: (1) current_user_id() allows identity spoofing (TST-2), so the filter runs on any user's notes; (2) the expression is passed directly to applyFilterExpression/eval (TST-1). Additionally, on any exception the response body includes a full Python traceback, leaking server internals. None of these paths have a test.
findings.fix:
test_filter_notes_valid_expression — POST /notes/filter with a benign expression, assert 200 and correct filtered results.
test_filter_notes_no_auth — POST without Authorization header, assert 401 or empty result (once auth is enforced).
test_filter_notes_eval_injection — POST with expression='__import__("os").getcwd()', assert 400 (not 200 or 500 with trace).
test_filter_notes_error_no_trace_leak — POST with a bad expression, assert the 500 response does NOT contain a 'trace' key.

findings.title: DELETE /notes/<id> route has no tests — 403 and 204 paths both unchecked
findings.why: The route is entirely new. No test verifies that a request without X-Admin-Token is rejected with 403, that a request with the correct token returns 204, or that the underlying delete_note is actually called. The only gate on the route (isAdmin) is itself untested (TST-3).
findings.fix:
test_remove_note_no_token_returns_403 — DELETE /notes/1 with no header, assert 403 and JSON body {"error": "forbidden"}.
test_remove_note_valid_token_returns_204 — DELETE /notes/1 with X-Admin-Token: letmein-admin, assert 204 and empty body.
test_remove_note_actually_deletes — seed a note, DELETE it with admin token, assert the row is absent in the DB.

findings.title: truncate ellipsis branch has no test (pre-existing gap, now more visible)
findings.why: The only existing test for truncate exercises the short-text branch (len <= length). The ellipsis branch (len > length) is unreachable by any test. This gap predates the PR but is surfaced here because truncate is called in the /notes/search response and its output contract is material to the API.
findings.fix: test_truncate_long_text_ellipsis — call truncate('a' * 200) and assert the result == 'a' * 140 + '...' and len(result) == 143.

not_checked: sample-project/config.py — only constant declarations; no logic paths to test
